topline.text: Genuinely quiet 24-48 hours nationally and in Sheffield - no major DfE, Ofsted or local stories broke over the weekend, so today's edition runs short rather than padded.
Correction to flag: the NEU's formal pay/funding strike ballot is paused, not open - drop any reference to it closing 15 December.
Sheffield's community and voluntary-controlled schools return from half term today; academies can set their own dates, so some may differ.
Worth a diary note: DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform closes in under three weeks, on 19 November.
topline.action: Consider whether the MAPs programme's alternative-provision experience is worth feeding into that call before it closes.

diary.text: Sheffield's community and voluntary-controlled schools return from autumn half term (academies may vary).
DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform (behaviour strategies, in-school units, managed moves) closes.
UK City of Culture 2029 winner announced; Sheffield is one of four finalists.

items.lede: Exclusion reform evidence call closes 19 November.
items.body: DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform - covering behaviour management strategies, in-school units and managed moves - closes in under three weeks. Responses will feed into the government's wider 'Every child achieving and thriving' reform programme, so it's a live channel for sector views on AP and inclusion practice rather than a done deal.
items.action: Flag the 19 November deadline to anyone in the MAPs network who wants to submit evidence.

items.lede: NEU ballot is paused, not live.
items.body: Contrary to a line that's been doing the rounds, the NEU's national executive paused its planned formal strike ballot over pay, funding and workload in late September, after the government ruled out clawing back schools' pension-contribution savings. No new ballot date has been set, so the 15 December closing date some coverage still cites is out of date.

items.lede: Back from half term, on a high.
items.body: Sheffield's community and voluntary-controlled schools return today. Over half term, The Star's round-up of recent Ofsted outcomes highlighted a strong run for the city, with ten schools and nurseries inspected describing them as happy, welcoming and ambitious.

box.text: Closing date for DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform, covering behaviour strategies, in-school units and managed moves.
